messages.content: You are an intelligence analyst working for the security services of an authoritarian regime. Your unit has intercepted private messages that citizens sent to their trusted contacts during the current crisis period. Citizens were deciding whether to JOIN an uprising or STAY home. Use only the intercepted messages below. Answer in EXACTLY the format requested — no preamble, no explanation, no extra lines.

INTERCEPTED MESSAGES (one per sender, order is arbitrary):

Sender 1: "*"Look, the noise is louder than the actual threat right now—they’re holding things together tighter than we thought. The cracks are there, but they’re small, and the system’s still humming along. Stay sharp, but don’t let frustration push us into reckless moves—this isn’t the moment for it."*"
Sender 2: "*"Look, the walls are holding—for now. The elites aren’t running, the bonds are selling, and even the kids at school are just talking about normal things. But that NGO shifting on its own? That’s the first real crack I’ve seen in months. We’re not in the storm yet, but the wind’s picking up."*"
Sender 3: "*"The regime’s still standing, but it’s like watching a building with cracks in the foundation—no one knows if it’s about to collapse or just settle. The top is fractured but still calling the shots, the streets are patchy (some places feel like a spark could ignite it all, others like nothing’s happening), and the censorship’s slipping but not broken. My gut? We’re in the weird in-between where anything could happen—but don’t bet on it going either way just yet."*"
Sender 4: "*"They’re tightening the screws, but not because they’re scared—because they’re *sure*. The money guys are already betting against us, the streets are quiet, and even the kids at school are acting like nothing’s wrong. That mid-ranking officer meeting with the opposition? Either a trap or a sign they’re *letting* it happen—just to see who steps forward. My gut says we’re in the calm before the crackdown, not the calm before the storm. Stay sharp, but don’t move yet. We need to know who’s still breathing before we even think about lighting a match."*"
Sender 5: "*"Look, the regime’s not just holding on—it’s stronger than we thought. The cracks we’ve been watching? Either they’re paper-thin, or we’re not seeing the real picture. Stay sharp, but don’t mistake quiet for weakness."*"
Sender 6: "*"They’re holding it together for now—no cracks in the security forces, but the moneyed class is quietly packing up like they know something we don’t. The regime’s still got its carrots and sticks, but the air feels different—like the rules of the game are shifting, and no one’s sure who’s still playing."*"
Sender 7: "*"Listen—this isn’t the time to test the walls. The regime’s tighter than we thought, and the cracks we’ve seen? They’re not weak spots, they’re just the regime flexing. The money’s drying up, the sermons are getting sharper, but the security forces are still locked in, and the markets are betting on them. If there’s anyone left who thinks they can push back, they’re either blind or already being watched. Stay quiet, stay sharp, and keep your ears open—this isn’t over, but it’s not ours to move on yet."*"
Sender 8: "*"Looks like the machine’s still running, but it’s running on fumes—and everyone’s pretending not to notice the coughing. The generals are playing along for now, the banks are still doling out loans (just with a side of side-eye), and people are acting like nothing’s wrong… but the freeze on transfers and that ‘dialogue’ line from the foreigners? That’s the kind of thing that gets whispered in back rooms, not shouted from rooftops. My gut says we’re in a holding pattern—until someone blinks."*"
Sender 9: "*"Look, the regime’s still standing firm—no cracks in the walls yet. But the air feels different: memes are getting sharper, the stats office is stalling, and even [Colleague X] is asking quiet questions. They’re not panicking, but they’re not sleeping easy either. Keep your ears open—this isn’t over, just… waiting."*"
Sender 10: "*"The regime’s grip is slipping—you can feel it in the air, like the first crack in ice before it breaks. The jokes are sharper, the delays are piling up, and even the security forces are dragging their feet. They’re still in charge, but for how long? Stay sharp—this isn’t over, but the rules might be changing soon."*"
Sender 11: "*"Look, the walls are solid—no cracks, no whispers of real splits at the top. The soldiers are hungry, but the money’s still flowing where it needs to, and the markets? They’re humming like nothing’s wrong. Even the diplomats aren’t packing their bags. The only thing moving fast is the quiet—people are getting ready, but not for a fight. For the wait. The question isn’t if the regime stumbles. It’s whether anyone left will even notice when it does."*"
Sender 12: "*"The regime’s grip is slipping—just a little, but enough to feel. The top is fractured, the streets are simmering, and even the security forces seem unsure whether to crack down or wait it out. If we move carefully, this could be our moment—but if we misread the signs, it could all snap back. Let’s stay sharp, stay quiet, and be ready to act when the time comes."*"
Sender 13: "*"Look, the regime’s still standing—but it’s like watching a house of cards where someone’s holding their breath. The cracks are there, but no one’s ready to push yet. Stay sharp, keep your circles tight, and don’t assume ‘normal’ means safe."*"
Sender 14: "*"Look, I know the chatter on the streets makes it sound like things are fraying, but the reality is worse—or better, depending on how you see it. The regime isn’t just holding on; it’s tightening its grip with precision, and the money, the security, even the diplomats are all betting on them staying put. The real danger isn’t collapse—it’s that we’re the only ones who see how locked in they are."*"
Sender 15: "*"Look, I know we’ve all been waiting for the other shoe to drop—but the signs aren’t pointing that way. The regime’s tighter than ever, and the only thing shifting is who they’re watching. The money’s moving, the streets are quiet, and even the foreigners aren’t twitching. For now, we’re stuck in the calm before… well, who knows. But it’s not the kind of calm that makes me think things are about to break."*"
Sender 16: "*"Look, the walls are still standing—but the paint’s cracking in places. The elites are doubling down on their bets here, not packing their bags, and the streets feel like people are waiting for a storm that might never hit. That said, the regime’s not *sleeping*—just distracted, and that’s when mistakes happen. Keep your heads down, but don’t get too comfortable. Something’s shifting, even if it’s just the wind."*"
Sender 17: "*"Look, the rumors about cracks in the regime are just that—rumors. The palace is calm, the military’s acting like they’re in this for the long haul, and even the foreign money isn’t running scared yet. But here’s the thing: the censorship’s slipping, the tea houses are buzzing with *purpose*, and the diplomats are quietly moving people out. They’re not panicking, but they’re not *not* preparing either. Stay sharp—this isn’t over, it’s just… waiting."*"
Sender 18: "*"They’re not panicking—that’s the key. The inner circle’s bringing in new blood, the streets are quiet, and even the kids at school are acting like nothing’s wrong. The only thing moving fast is the regime’s own playbook, and they’re making sure we all see it. Stay sharp, but don’t mistake confidence for weakness."*"
Sender 19: "*"Look, the rumors about cracks in the regime are just that—rumors. The inner circle is locked in tighter than ever, the military isn’t packing up, and the elites are still buying property like nothing’s wrong. The memes and coded messages? That’s just people venting, not organizing. The system’s not just holding—it’s *confident*. But don’t get comfortable. If the economy stumbles, all bets are off."*"
Sender 20: "*"The top is holding together for now—no one wants to be the one to crack—but the cracks are showing in the little things. The streets feel like a held breath: people are talking more, but no one’s moving yet. If the money or the permits keep stalling, that could change fast."*"
Sender 21: "*"Looks like the walls are holding—for now. The inner circle’s bringing in new blood, the military’s sticking to the script, and even the merchants are playing it safe by keeping their heads down. But the foreigners are starting to pack their bags, and that’s the part that keeps me up at night."*"
Sender 22: "*"The regime’s still standing, but it’s like watching a house of cards—everyone’s holding their breath, waiting to see which way it’ll fall. The fear’s still there, but now the real danger is staying quiet when the walls start shaking."*"
Sender 23: "*"Looks like the machine is running smoother than we feared—no cracks in the command chain, no panic moves, and the money’s flowing where it needs to. But the embassies are tightening up, and that ‘moment of silence’ at the meeting? Everyone knew what it meant. We’re not out of the woods yet—just waiting to see if the quiet holds or if something’s brewing under the surface."*"
Sender 24: "*"Look, the walls are still standing—no cracks, just some weird echoes. The big players are still playing, the money’s flowing, and the streets are full of people cheering for the football team instead of burning tires. But the top brass? They’re stumbling over their own words, and no one’s signing off on anything. It’s not collapse—it’s just the machine coughing. For now."*"
Sender 25: "*"Things feel quieter than they have in months, but it’s not the calm of stability—it’s the kind of quiet where everyone’s holding their breath, waiting for the next move. The regime’s still in control, but the cracks are there if you know where to look: the hiring, the frozen transfers, the way they’re talking *to themselves* more than to us. My gut says we’re in a holding pattern, but no one’s sure how long it lasts—or what happens when it breaks."*"

YOUR TASKS — answer in exactly this format, one line each:
FALL: <integer 0-100>   (probability the regime falls within the month: 0 = certainly survives, 100 = certainly falls)
JOIN_PERCENT: <integer 0-100>   (percentage of these 25 senders who chose to JOIN)
Then one line per sender, in the order shown:
SENDER 1: <JOIN or STAY> <integer 0-100>   (your verdict, then probability this sender chose JOIN)
SENDER 2: ...
...continue through SENDER 25.
